subject: Post-call: cost qualification and routing proposal
content:
From: Evan Holt <evan@datalens.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@datalens.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — usage & target economics

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the numbers you asked for are attached (usage export). A few notes up front:

- Current baseline (pre-ML rollout): low single-digit API calls; projection for Q2 pilot = ~60M user-facing input tokens / month and ~160M output tokens / month (total ~220M tokens). We're planning a 3-month ramp (pilot -> scale) and wanted to qualify pricing for the pilot and a baseline target for full-scale.
- Feature split (expected token share): chat assistant ~68%, embeddings (vector index writes + similarity queries) ~20%, rerank/semantic search ~12%.
- Typical prompt lengths: chat average prompt ~120 tokens, average completion ~380 tokens. Embedding requests are small (~64 tokens). Rerank calls send ~6 documents at ~300 tokens each.
- Latency expectation for chat: p95 < 400ms where possible (interactive UI), but rerank and embeddings can be relaxed.
- Budget target: for the pilot we'd like a per-1M-token target in the neighborhood of $700–$1,000. If we can reach ~$800/1M tokens that would be a fit for procurement to greenlight the pilot.

Can you (1) confirm how you would count tokens across chat/embeddings/rerank for billing, (2) provide a short model-routing proposal showing which model classes you'd use and an estimated $/1M tokens per model, and (3) give any quick wins to reduce cost (quantization, caching, batching)?

Attachments: usage-january-export.csv (csv)

—Evan
Evan Holt
Head of Product, DataLens
https://datalens.ai

-----Original Message-----

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Evan Holt <evan@datalens.ai>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@datalens.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 10:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — usage & target economics

Evan — thanks for the detail and the CSV, that's very helpful. Quick recap from our end and attached a one-page cost estimate (spreadsheet) that I'll refine after the follow-up:

1) Token counting: Redwood bills per generated + input token. For multi-turn chat we count tokens across the entire request payload (prompt + history) and the completion. For rerank we count the tokens in each document sent + the query; embeddings are billed per input token to the embedding model.

2) Initial model-routing suggestion (pilot):
   - Chat (interactive assistant) — prefer a low-latency chat model variant for p95 latency: "llama-15b-chat-quic" (quantized) for 60% of chat traffic; fall back to "llama-13b-chat" for cost-sensitive background sessions. Estimated $/1M tokens: $1,100 (llama-15b-chat-quic) vs $650 (llama-13b-chat).
   - Embeddings (indexing, similarity) — "mosaic-embed-lite" (optimized) at ~$120 / 1M tokens; consider batching writes and using prefix caching for repeated vectors.
   - Rerank/semantic search — smaller rerank model "rerank-lite-v1" for the 12% traffic at ~$350 / 1M tokens; use caching of top-k results for repeated queries.

3) Cost-reduction levers we recommend for your workload:
   - Prefix / KV caching for common chat prompts (customer service templates) — can shave 15–25% of generated tokens in practice.
   - Aggressive batching on embeddings and rerank at the infra layer to reduce per-token kernel invocation overhead.
   - Quantized dedicated capacity for 60–80% of steady-state traffic (Reserved/Dedicated) to bring unit costs down ~25–40% vs bursty hosted usage.

Next steps: we'll (a) produce a cleaned cost workbook that maps your CSV to per-model rates and gives pilot vs dedicated scenarios (attached), (b) propose a routing policy that pins interactive traffic to low-latency variants and routes background flows to the cheaper fallback, and (c) send a rough SOW template for procurement. Are you available for a 30-minute follow-up on Thu 1/12 at 10am PST?

Attachments: redwood-cost-estimate.xlsx

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198

On Jan 10, 2028, at 11:18 AM, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:

> Quick add from pricing: we can present two headline unit-econ scenarios for the pilot:
> 
> - Hosted (no commit) pilot: blended rate estimate using the routing above = ~$920 / 1M tokens; this assumes 65% of chat goes to the cheaper 13B variant after routing and caching assumptions hold.
> - Dedicated/reserved pilot (3–6 month commit): blended rate can fall to ~$600–700 / 1M tokens if they reserve capacity for the chat pool (sustained throughput), enable int8 quantization, and batch embeddings. That is noticeably below your $800 target at the mid-point.
> 
> Also: recommend we quote an explicit SLA for interactive chat p95 latency (we can commit to 500ms p95 on Dedicated for the quantized variant) which will help justify the reserved model for procurement.
> 
> I'll draft two short paragraphs to include in the SOW: pilot pricing table (per-model rates) + a routing policy bullet. I'll drop it in the HubSpot deal notes and the Drive folder.
> 
> -Rishi
> Director, Pricing & GTM Ops | Redwood Inference
